tasks.title: Adopt a written operating agreement
tasks.why: Texas does not file it, but banks ask for it and it is what separates the entity from its owner if that separation is ever tested.
have_ready: What happens if an owner leaves
common_mistakes: Skipping it because a single-member LLC 'does not need one' - the bank will still ask.

tasks.title: Apply for an EIN from the IRS
tasks.why: The EIN is the business's tax identity and is required to open a business bank account without using a Social Security number.

sources.title: IRS - Apply for an EIN Online

have_ready: Exact legal entity name as filed
common_mistakes: Paying a service for this. The IRS issues an EIN at no charge and the online application takes minutes.
Applying before the entity is formed, which produces an EIN attached to the wrong name.

tasks.title: Open a business bank account
tasks.why: Commingling personal and business funds is the most common way the liability separation an LLC provides gets argued away.
common_mistakes: Running revenue through a personal account 'just until things settle'.

tasks.title: Set up a Texas franchise tax account with the Comptroller
tasks.why: Texas LLCs owe an annual franchise tax report even in years when no tax is due, and the report is what keeps the entity in good standing.

deadline.rule: Annual report is due each May 15 for the prior reporting year.

common_mistakes: Assuming no tax due means no filing due. The report is still required.

tasks.title: Obtain professional liability and general liability insurance
tasks.why: An LLC limits owner liability for business debts; it does not cover a claim arising from the work itself.
common_mistakes: Assuming the entity itself is the insurance.

decisions.title: 'LLC or S-corp' is two separate questions wearing one coat
decisions.context: First-time founders almost always arrive asking whether to form an LLC or an S-corp, and the question has no answer as posed because the two words describe different layers of the stack.
decisions.common_misconception: That an LLC and an S-corp are two entity types to pick between.

options.name: LLC (state legal entity)
options.what_it_actually_is: A legal entity created by filing with a state. It determines who is liable for the business's obligations.
options.consequence: By default a single-member LLC is taxed as a sole proprietorship: profit flows to a Schedule C and is subject to self-employment tax.

options.name: S-corp (federal tax election)
options.what_it_actually_is: An election filed with the IRS on Form 2553 that changes how an existing LLC or corporation is taxed. It creates no entity.
options.consequence: Profit splits into reasonable salary plus distribution, which changes the self-employment tax base, and it adds payroll administration and a separate business return.

decisions.what_actually_differs: The entity decision and the tax-treatment decision are made at different times, with different agencies, on different deadlines. An LLC can make the S-corp election later; the election cannot exist without an entity under it.
depends_on_facts: What counts as reasonable salary for this work in this market
Cost of payroll administration and a second tax return
Whether the 2553 window for the intended tax year is still open
decisions.consequences: Treating these as one decision is how founders either form an entity they did not need or miss an election window they did. The two decisions are sequenced, not traded off.
decisions.professional_question: Given my projected profit, at what point does the self-employment tax saved by an S-corp election exceed the payroll and filing cost it adds?

sources.title: IRS - About Form 2553, Election by a Small Business Corporation

decisions.title: Forming in Delaware while living and working in Texas
decisions.context: Delaware's reputation as the default state of incorporation comes from venture-backed C-corps, and it propagates to solo founders whose situation does not resemble that one.
decisions.common_misconception: That Delaware formation is a neutral default with no cost.

options.name: Form in Texas
options.what_it_actually_is: One filing, one state, one annual report, and the registered agent can be the founder at a Texas street address.
options.consequence: One set of fees and one set of deadlines.

options.name: Form in Delaware, operate from Texas
options.what_it_actually_is: A Delaware entity that transacts business in Texas generally must also register in Texas as a foreign entity.
options.consequence: Two states' fees, two annual obligations, and a registered agent in Delaware who must be paid because the founder is not there.

decisions.what_actually_differs: Whether the business pays one state or two for the same operation, and whether a paid registered agent becomes mandatory.
depends_on_facts: Whether outside investors have asked for a Delaware entity
Where the work is actually performed
Delaware franchise tax and registered agent cost at current rates
decisions.consequences: For a founder whose customers, work, and residence are all in one state, the second state adds recurring cost and a second calendar without changing the liability outcome.
decisions.professional_question: Does anything in my funding plan over the next 24 months require a Delaware entity, and what does it cost to convert later if it does?

elections.name: S corporation election
elections.what_it_does: Changes how an existing LLC's profit is taxed by splitting it into reasonable salary and distribution, which changes the self-employment tax base.

sources.title: IRS - About Form 2553, Election by a Small Business Corporation

eligibility: A domestic entity with allowable shareholders
One class of stock or equivalent membership interest

sources.title: IRS - About Form 2553, Election by a Small Business Corporation

deadline.rule: No more than two months and fifteen days after the beginning of the tax year the election is to take effect, or at any time during the preceding tax year.

elections.admin_cost_note: Adds payroll administration and a separate business return.
elections.lost_if_missed: The election generally takes effect the following tax year instead, so a missed window costs a full year of whatever the election was worth.
elections.professional_question: At my projected profit, does this election clear its own administrative cost this year?

elections.name: Business start-up cost deduction
elections.what_it_does: Allows a portion of costs incurred investigating and setting up the business before it opened to be deducted, with the remainder amortized.
eligibility: Costs incurred before the business began operating
Costs would have been deductible had the business already been active

deadline.rule: Claimed on the return for the tax year the business begins operating.

elections.lost_if_missed: Receipts discarded before launch cannot be reconstructed later, so this is lost by inaction rather than by decision.
elections.professional_question: Which of my pre-launch costs qualify, and how should I be recording them starting today?

elections.name: Business use of home deduction
elections.what_it_does: Allows a portion of home expenses to be attributed to a space used regularly and exclusively as the principal place of business.
eligibility: Regular and exclusive business use of the space
The space is the principal place of business
elections.lost_if_missed: Contemporaneous records of the space and its use are far harder to assemble after the fact than to keep from the start.
elections.professional_question: Does my workspace meet the regular-and-exclusive test, and which calculation method fits my situation?

elections.name: Solo 401(k) or SEP plan
elections.what_it_does: Creates a retirement plan for an owner-only business, with contribution room well above an individual retirement account.
eligibility: No employees other than a spouse

sources.title: IRS - About Publication 560, Retirement Plans for Small Business

deadline.rule: Plan establishment and funding deadlines differ by plan type and are tied to the business's tax year and return due date.

elections.lost_if_missed: A plan not established within its window cannot be applied retroactively to that tax year.
